This section examines Experiment M —
Eight-module LLM landscape from

first principles. Keep two questions
separate: does changing the order

change the measured outcome, and does the
proposed search method

beat a matched alternative at the same
distinct-evaluation budget? Search

space: 8!=40,320 possible prompts.
Evaluation: 20 G S M eight

K questions; Gemini Flash-Lite; 23,805
cached calls; reported spend $5.56;

hard cost cap. Sample: 222 unbiased
completed orderings for diagnostics.

Gate result: accuracy 0.10–1.00, standard
deviation 0.240. Pre-flight:

insert rho_1=0.75; approximate F D C =
−0.095, predicting random

competitiveness. Search: prism and random
both reached 1.000 at every

tested budget in the four-seed search
stage. Lesson: only 20

questions made the accuracy grid coarse
and exact optima dense.

Measurement resolution must be selected
before search spend. Now read

evidence panel M-eight-module. The axes,
units, and sample are stated

on screen. The sample represented here is
20 questions. Raw

observations remain visible wherever the
artifact provides them. Censored

observations stay marked at the cap rather
than becoming invented

hitting times, and sampled landscapes
leave unobserved permutations blank.

The supported finding is: Gate result:
accuracy 0.10–1.00, standard

established here is: Lesson:

only 20 questions made the accuracy grid
coarse and exact

optima dense. This evidence changed the
program as follows: Carry

and compare methods at

result. A

large ordering effect does not
automatically imply an evolutionary-search

advantage, and almost-sure convergence
does not promise practical
efficiency.
